questions.question: Geography challenge: Which country is doubly landlocked (only landlocked neighbors)?
questions.note: Mongolia borders Russia and China, both with coasts.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which is the world's fourth most populous country?
questions.note: After India, China, and the United States.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Monsoons are driven mainly by…?

choices.C: Uneven heating of land and sea

questions.note: Land heats and cools faster than sea, reversing winds by season.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which line marks the northernmost point where the Sun can be directly overhead?
questions.note: About 23.4° N, reached at the June solstice.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Fjords are formed mainly by…?
questions.note: Glacial valleys later flooded by the sea.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which country has coastlines on both the Caribbean Sea and the Pacific Ocean?
questions.note: Venezuela is Caribbean only; Ecuador and Peru are Pacific only.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which 'sea' is actually the world's largest lake?
questions.note: It is landlocked, about 371,000 km².

questions.question: Geography challenge: The Strait of Malacca separates which two countries?
questions.note: Peninsular Malaysia and Sumatra. The Johor Strait separates Malaysia and Singapore.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Counting overseas territories, which country has the most time zones?
questions.note: France has 12 (13 with its Antarctic claim); Russia and the U.S. have 11.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which African river crosses the Equator twice?
questions.note: Its arc runs north then back south of the Equator.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which South American country does NOT border Brazil?
questions.note: Only Chile and Ecuador lack a border with Brazil.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Why do coastal cities usually have smaller temperature swings than inland ones?
questions.note: Oceans warm and cool slowly, moderating nearby air.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which continent is crossed by both the Equator and the Prime Meridian?
questions.note: They intersect in the Gulf of Guinea, off Africa.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which country lies entirely south of the Equator?
questions.note: Kenya, Indonesia, and Colombia all straddle the Equator.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which major river flows mostly northward?
questions.note: It flows north to the Mediterranean.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which country's capital lies on the Danube?
questions.note: Budapest. Prague is on the Vltava, Warsaw the Vistula, Bucharest the Dâmbovița.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which is the largest country located entirely in Europe?
questions.note: About 603,000 km². Russia, Kazakhstan, and Turkey span two continents.

questions.question: Geography challenge: The point at 0° latitude, 0° longitude lies in which body of water?
questions.note: Off the coast of West Africa.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which of these cities lies farthest north?
questions.note: Rome ~41.9° N, New York ~40.7°, Madrid ~40.4°, Beijing ~39.9°.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which river drains into the Indian Ocean rather than the Atlantic?
questions.note: The Zambezi reaches the sea in Mozambique.

questions.question: Geography challenge: On the December solstice, which city has the longest daylight?
questions.note: It is southern summer, and Buenos Aires (~34.6° S) is farthest south of the Equator.

questions.question: Geography challenge: A ship going through the Panama Canal from the Atlantic to the Pacific travels generally…?
questions.note: The canal's Atlantic end (Colón) is northwest of its Pacific end.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which capital city is closest to the Equator?
questions.note: Quito ~0.2° S, Nairobi ~1.3° S, Singapore ~1.3° N, Jakarta ~6.2° S.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which country borders both the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf?
questions.note: Iran's north coast is on the Caspian, its south on the Gulf.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which country's territory is the first to enter each new calendar day?
questions.note: Kiribati's Line Islands use UTC+14.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Besides Uganda, which two countries border Lake Victoria?
questions.note: Tanzania holds about half the lake.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which country has NO Mediterranean coastline?
questions.note: Portugal faces only the Atlantic; Slovenia and Bosnia have short Adriatic coasts.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Going straight through Earth's center from Manila, you would surface in…?
questions.note: Manila's antipode is near 14.6° S, 59° W, in central South America.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which is the largest ocean?
questions.note: The Pacific covers about a third of Earth's surface.

questions.question: Geography challenge: What is the capital of Japan?
questions.note: Kyoto was the imperial capital until 1868.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which river flows through the world's largest rainforest?
questions.note: The Amazon basin holds the largest tropical rainforest.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which country has the most people in South America?
questions.note: Brazil has over 200 million people.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Mount Everest is part of which mountain range?
questions.note: K2 is in the Karakoram.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which desert covers much of northern Africa?
questions.note: The Kalahari is in southern Africa; the Gobi is in Asia.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which country is shaped like a boot?
questions.note: The Italian peninsula's shape resembles a boot.

questions.question: Geography challenge: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.note: Canberra was purpose-built as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which is the largest country by area?
questions.note: About 17.1 million km²; Canada is second.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which line divides Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres?
questions.note: The Prime Meridian divides East and West.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which river flows through Baghdad?
questions.note: The Euphrates runs parallel to the west.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which country contains most of the Atacama Desert?
questions.note: Northern Chile, along the Pacific coast.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which African country has the largest population?
questions.note: Nigeria has over 200 million people.

questions.question: Geography challenge: The Strait of Gibraltar connects the Atlantic Ocean with the…?
questions.note: It separates Spain from Morocco.

questions.question: Geography challenge: What is the smallest country in the world by area?
questions.note: About 0.44 km²; Monaco is second.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which country does NOT border Germany?
questions.note: Austria and Switzerland separate Germany from Italy.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Mount Kilimanjaro is in which country?
questions.note: It sits near the Kenyan border but inside Tanzania.

questions.question: Geography challenge: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.note: Toronto is Canada's largest city.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which body of water lies between Saudi Arabia and northeast Africa?
questions.note: The Persian Gulf is on Saudi Arabia's east side.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which U.S. state is the largest by area?
questions.note: Alaska is more than twice the size of Texas.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which country has the world's longest coastline?
questions.note: About 202,000 km including its Arctic islands.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which country is completely surrounded by South Africa?
questions.note: Eswatini also borders Mozambique.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which two countries share the world's longest land border?
questions.note: About 8,900 km; Russia–Kazakhstan is second.

questions.question: Geography challenge: The Danube River empties into which sea?
questions.note: Its delta is on the Romania–Ukraine coast.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which city lies on two continents?
questions.note: The Bosporus splits it between Europe and Asia.

questions.question: Geography challenge: What is the capital of Brazil?
questions.note: Brasília replaced Rio de Janeiro as capital in 1960.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
questions.note: Over 1,600 m deep, in Siberia.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which north–south range forms much of the conventional Europe–Asia boundary?
questions.note: The Caucasus run east–west further south.

questions.question: Geography challenge: What is the largest island that is not a continent?
questions.note: About 2.17 million km²; New Guinea is second.

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which river forms much of the U.S.–Mexico border?
questions.note: Called the Río Bravo in Mexico.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What is the chemical formula for water?
questions.note: H₂O₂ is hydrogen peroxide.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.note: Venus is second.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
questions.note: Plants release oxygen as a by-product.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which part of an animal cell holds most of its DNA?
questions.note: Ribosomes build proteins; the membrane encloses the cell.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which force keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun?
questions.note: Inertia alone would send planets off in straight lines.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: At sea level, water boils at what temperature?
questions.note: Equal to 212 °F.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.note: Jupiter is over 300 times Earth's mass.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What is the hardest natural substance?
questions.note: Diamond is 10 on the Mohs scale.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: How many bones are in the adult human body?
questions.note: Babies have about 270–300 that fuse over time.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What kind of animal is a whale?
questions.note: Whales breathe air and nurse their young.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which organ produces insulin?
questions.note: Insulin comes from beta cells in the pancreas.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What is the most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere?
questions.note: About 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which plant-cell part carries out photosynthesis?
questions.note: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
questions.note: From Latin 'natrium'. S is sulfur.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Through which material does sound travel fastest?
questions.note: Sound is fastest in solids and cannot travel through a vacuum.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which blood cells fight infection?
questions.note: Red cells carry oxygen; platelets help clotting.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which planet has the hottest surface?
questions.note: Venus's thick CO₂ atmosphere traps heat (~465 °C), hotter than Mercury.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which subatomic particle has a negative charge?
questions.note: Protons and positrons are positive; neutrons are neutral.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which type of rock forms when magma cools?
questions.note: Clastic rocks are a kind of sedimentary rock.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What is the pH of pure water at 25 °C?
questions.note: Neutral is pH 7.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Why do we see lightning before we hear thunder?
questions.note: Both occur together; light arrives almost instantly.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which gas forms when baking soda reacts with vinegar?
questions.note: An acid–base reaction releases CO₂ bubbles.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
questions.note: Veins return blood to the heart.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which element has atomic number 6?
questions.note: Boron is 5, nitrogen 7, oxygen 8.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: In which atmospheric layer is the ozone layer found?
questions.note: Roughly 15–35 km up.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What type of energy does a stretched rubber band store?
questions.note: Released as kinetic energy when let go.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What is the shape of a DNA molecule?
questions.note: Described by Watson and Crick in 1953.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which planet has the shortest day?
questions.note: Jupiter rotates in about 10 hours; Saturn in about 10.7.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which vitamin does your skin make in sunlight?
questions.note: UVB light triggers vitamin D production.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which of these is a noble gas?
questions.note: Noble gases (group 18) are very unreactive.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What causes the Moon's phases?

choices.C: Our changing view of its lit half

questions.note: Earth's shadow on the Moon is a lunar eclipse, not a phase.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Compared with on Earth, an astronaut's mass on the Moon is…?
questions.note: Weight drops to about one-sixth; mass does not change.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Ignoring air resistance, a bowling ball and a tennis ball are dropped together. Which lands first?
questions.note: Gravity accelerates all objects equally.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Why does ice float on liquid water?

choices.B: It is less dense than water

questions.note: Water expands when it freezes.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which process releases energy from glucose inside cells?
questions.note: It takes place mainly in mitochondria.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What happens to water's boiling point at high altitude?
questions.note: Lower air pressure lets water boil at a lower temperature.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Why is the daytime sky blue?
questions.note: Rayleigh scattering affects shorter wavelengths most.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: In a simple series circuit, if one bulb burns out, the other bulbs…?
questions.note: A series circuit has only one path; a break stops all current.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which of these is a chemical change?
questions.note: Rust is a new substance (iron oxide). The others are physical changes.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What mainly causes Earth's seasons?
questions.note: Earth is actually closest to the Sun in January.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: A ball thrown straight up reaches its highest point. Its acceleration there is…?
questions.note: Velocity is zero at the top, but gravity still accelerates it.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which blood type is the universal donor for red blood cells?
questions.note: AB positive is the universal recipient.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: At the same room temperature, why does a metal spoon feel colder than a wooden one?
questions.note: Both are the same temperature; metal draws heat from your hand faster.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What happens to an animal cell placed in very salty water?
questions.note: Osmosis moves water out toward the saltier side.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which planet is less dense than water?
questions.note: Saturn's average density is about 0.69 g/cm³.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Two 6-ohm resistors connected in parallel have a total resistance of…?
Scientific knowledge check: Why do astronauts float aboard the International Space Station?

choices.A: They are in continuous free fall
choices.B: There is no gravity in orbit

questions.note: Gravity at ISS height is still about 90% of surface gravity.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: B is dominant over b. If both parents are Bb, what is the chance a child is bb?
questions.note: Punnett square: BB, Bb, bB, bb — one in four.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: As a siren moves away from you, its pitch sounds…?
questions.note: The Doppler effect stretches the sound waves.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Why don't antibiotics cure the common cold?
questions.note: Antibiotics target bacteria, not viruses.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: A rock weighs 30 N in air and 20 N fully underwater. Its density is how many times water's?
questions.note: Buoyant force = 10 N = weight of equal-volume water, so 30 ÷ 10 = 3.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: When light passes from air into water, its speed and wavelength…?
questions.note: Frequency stays constant, so wavelength shrinks with speed.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: An object moves in a circle at constant speed. Why is it accelerating?
questions.note: Acceleration is any change in velocity, including direction.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which is the strongest evidence the continents were once joined?
questions.note: Fossils like Mesosaurus appear in both South America and Africa.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which has more total thermal energy?
questions.note: Temperature is average energy per particle; the tub has far more water.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: If Earth had no Moon, ocean tides would…?
questions.note: The Sun would still cause tides, about half as strong.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: An isotope's half-life is 10 years. What fraction remains after 30 years?
Scientific knowledge check: Which element most readily forms a +1 ion?
questions.note: Alkali metals lose one electron. Mg forms +2; Cl and O form negative ions.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: If a car's speed doubles, its kinetic energy becomes…?
questions.note: KE = ½mv², so doubling v quadruples KE.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Why does air in the lower atmosphere get colder as you climb, despite being nearer the Sun?

choices.B: It is heated mainly from the ground

questions.note: Sunlight warms the surface, which warms the air above it.
